title: Open extension by zero and restriction for graded sheaf modules
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $\mathcal A=(\mathcal A^i)_{i\in\mathbf Z}$ be a family of $\mathcal O$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with associative $\mathcal O$-bilinear multiplications $\mathcal A^i\times\mathcal A^j\to\mathcal A^{i+j}$ and a two-sided identity section $1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal A^0)$. Write $\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)$ for families $M^q$ of $\mathcal O$-module sheaves with associative unital $\mathcal O$-bilinear left actions $\mathcal A^i\times M^q\to M^{i+q}$ and action-preserving degree-zero $\mathcal O$-linear maps. No differential is included in these objects or maps. For an open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ put $\mathcal A_U=\mathcal A|_U$. For $L\in\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A_U)$ define the graded presheaf $P_L$ by $P_L^q(V)=L^q(V)$ for $V\subseteq U$ and $P_L^q(V)=0$ otherwise. Restrictions are those of $L$ when the source open is contained in $U$ and zero otherwise; the $\mathcal A(V)$-action is the restricted given action or the zero action. Sheafify each degree as an $\mathcal O$-module [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The resulting sheaves carry the induced graded left $\mathcal A$-action and define a functor $j_!: \operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A_U)\to\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)$. Its restriction to $U$ is canonically $L$. Restriction of a map to $U$ under this identification gives a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)}(j_!L,M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A_U)}(L,M|_U).$$

source.place: Tag 0FRA (lemma-extension-by-zero-graded), section-localize-graded, specialized to the open site of a topological space and degree-zero left-module maps; the preceding degreewise construction. Left actions are the left analogue of definition-gm (Tag 0FQZ), as explicitly allowed immediately after that definition.

proof.text: The stated $P_L$ is a graded presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules: composable restrictions with source in $U$ are those of $L$, while a source outside $U$ gives a zero map, as does the composite. The same cases verify semilinearity and compatibility of the presheaf actions with restrictions. Let $E^q=(P_L^q)^\#$ and write $\theta_q:P_L^q\to E^q$. Module sheafification supplies these sheaves, linear unit maps, and their universal factorization property. It also supplies the degreewise maps $E(f)^q$ induced by a morphism $f:L\to L'$, with $E(f)^q\theta_q=\theta'_qP_f^q$.

source.place: section-localize-graded, degreewise construction preceding lemma-extension-by-zero-graded (Tag 0FRA); module sheafification as in Tag 03CY

proof.text: For every $i,q$, compose the presheaf action with $\theta_{i+q}$ to obtain a restriction-compatible bilinear pairing $\mathcal A^i\times P_L^q\to E^{i+q}$. Apply bilinear extension to this pairing over the already sheaf ring $\mathcal O$. Since $\mathcal A^i$ is already a sheaf, its sheafification is itself (the inverse to its unit is the unique factorization of its identity, with both inverse equations following by uniqueness). We obtain $\mu_{i,q}:\mathcal A^i\times E^q\to E^{i+q}$ with the explicit equation $\mu_{i,q}(a,\theta_q(p))=\theta_{i+q}(ap)$. The extension is unique, bilinear, and compatible with restrictions.

source.place: section-localize-graded, construction of multiplication on extension by zero, left-module version; Tag 0GMW supplies bilinear extension

proof.text: We will use uniqueness also after restriction to any open $V\subseteq X$. The inclusion of the open site of $V$ in that of $X$ is continuous: an open cover stays a cover. It is cocontinuous: any cover of an open $W\subseteq V$ in $X$ consists of opens still contained in $V$, and hence is the same cover in $V$. The sites are small in the fixed universe convention. The restriction/sheafification comparison therefore says that $E^q|_V$ is the module sheafification of $P_L^q|_V$, with precisely the restricted unit $\theta_q|_V$. Consequently two linear maps from $E^q|_V$ agree if they agree after this unit. At $V=U$, $P_L^q|_U=L^q$ is already a sheaf; its unit is invertible by the universal property. The equation in step 2 identifies the restricted action with the given action of $L$. Thus $E|_U\cong L$ as graded modules, canonically and naturally in $L$.

source.place: lemma-extension-by-zero-graded (Tag 0FRA), localization identifications; restriction comparison from Tag 04B8

proof.text: Check the graded module laws without assuming any commutativity of $\mathcal A$. On an arbitrary open $V$, fix $a\in\mathcal A^i(V)$ and $b\in\mathcal A^j(V)$. The maps $x\mapsto\mu_{i+j,q}(ab,x)$ and $x\mapsto\mu_{i,j+q}(a,\mu_{j,q}(b,x))$ are linear sheaf maps $E^q|_V\to E^{i+j+q}|_V$, using restrictions of $a,b$ on smaller opens. On $\theta_q(p)$ their values are respectively $\theta_{i+j+q}((ab)p)$ and $\theta_{i+j+q}(a(bp))$, equal by associativity of the presheaf action (the zero module case outside $U$ included). Restricted uniqueness from step 3 proves equality. Likewise $x\mapsto\mu_{0,q}(1,x)$ and the identity agree on $\theta_q(p)$, so agree everywhere. Bilinearity was supplied in step 2. Thus $E$ is an object of $\operatorname{Gr}(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: section-localize-graded, verification that the degreewise construction is a graded module (Tag 0FRA)

proof.text: For a graded module map $f:L\to L'$, compare the two bilinear maps $\mathcal A^i\times E^q\to E'^{i+q}$ given by $E(f)^{i+q}\mu_{i,q}$ and $\mu'_{i,q}(1\times E(f)^q)$. Precomposing with $1\times\theta_q$, both give $\theta'_{i+q}f(ap)=\theta'_{i+q}(a f(p))$. Uniqueness of bilinear extension makes the maps equal, proving action compatibility. Degreewise sheafification uniqueness shows $E(1)=1$ and $E(gf)=E(g)E(f)$: the two sides have identical composites with every $\theta_q$. This constructs the functor $j_!$ with the specified degreewise construction.

source.place: section-localize-graded, construction on homogeneous maps, specialized to degree zero (Tag 0FRA)

proof.text: Given $h:L\to M|_U$ in graded modules, define $\widetilde h^q:P_L^q\to M^q$ by $h^q_V$ for $V\subseteq U$ and by zero otherwise. This is a linear presheaf map: for a restriction whose source is outside $U$, both composites are zero; the remaining case is naturality of $h$. Its action equation holds on opens in $U$ by that of $h$, and elsewhere because the input from $P_L^q$ is zero. Sheafification yields a unique $\bar h^q:E^q\to M^q$ with $\bar h^q\theta_q=\widetilde h^q$. The bilinear maps $(a,x)\mapsto\bar h^{i+q}(\mu_{i,q}(a,x))$ and $(a,x)\mapsto a\bar h^q(x)$ agree on $\mathcal A^i\times P_L^q$ by this equation and the presheaf action equation. Bilinear-extension uniqueness proves equality on $\mathcal A^i\times E^q$. Hence $\bar h$ is a graded module map. This explicitly fills the obstruction-compatibility check omitted in the proof of Tag 0FRA.

source.place: lemma-extension-by-zero-graded (Tag 0FRA), omitted action-compatibility verification, degree-zero left-module form

proof.text: Restriction of a graded map $g:E\to M$, using $E|_U\cong L$ from step 3, gives $h=(g\theta)|_U$. Extending this $h$ by step 6 returns $g$: on opens contained in $U$ the composites with $\theta$ agree by definition, and on other opens $P_L$ is zero, so they also agree there; module sheafification uniqueness gives equality. Conversely $\bar h\theta=\widetilde h$ restricts on $U$ to $h$, proving the other inverse equation. For $f:L'\to L$ and $k:M\to M'$, the presheaf formula gives $\widetilde{(k|_U)hf}=k\widetilde h P_f$; uniqueness yields $\overline{(k|_U)hf}=k\bar h\,j_!(f)$. Thus the inverse bijections are natural in both variables and are exactly the restriction map in the statement.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0FRA (lemma-extension-by-zero-graded) and its preceding degreewise construction, specialized to a topological space and left actions; the omitted compatibility is expanded via bilinear sheafification uniqueness (Tag 0GMW), with restriction of sheafification (Tag 04B8).

lean.statement: theorem exists_openExtensionAdjunction : ∃ (E : Module.{u, u, w, max u w} (A.over U) ⥤ Module.{u, u, w, max u w} A) (e : ∀ q : ℤ, E ⋙ evaluation A q ≅ openExtensionDegree A U q) (ρ : E ⋙ restriction A U ≅ 𝟭 (Module.{u, u, w, max u w} (A.over U))) (adj : E ⊣ restriction A U), (∀ (L : Module.{u, u, w, max u w} (A.over U)) (i q : ℤ) (V : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (φ : V.unop ⟶ U) (a : (A.degree i).val.obj V) (x : (L.degree q).val.obj (op (Over.mk φ))), (E.obj L).act i q V a (openExtensionUnit A U E e L q V φ x) = openExtensionUnit A U E e L (i + q) V φ (L.act i q (op (Over.mk φ)) a x)) ∧ (∀ (L : Module.{u, u, w, max u w} (A.over U)) (q : ℤ) (V : (Opens X)ᵒᵖ) (φ : V.unop ⟶ U) (x : (L.degree q).val.obj (op (Over.mk φ))), ((ρ.hom.app L).degree q).val.app (op (Over.mk φ)) (openExtensionUnit A U E e L q V φ x) = x) ∧ (∀ (L : Module.{u, u, w, max u w} (A.over U)) (M : Module.{u, u, w, max u w} A) (g : E.obj L ⟶ M), adj.homEquiv L M g = ρ.inv.app L ≫ (restriction A U).map g)
